question: What type of engine is the CFM56-7B?

options.text: A triple spool, low bypass turbofan
A twin spool, axial flow, high bypass turbofan
A single spool, centrifugal flow turbojet
A geared turbofan with a single spool core

explanation: The high bypass layout produces most of its thrust from the fan, which is what gives the efficiency and the noise levels of a modern narrowbody.

question: Which components make up the N1 spool?

options.text: The fan and the high pressure compressor
The high pressure compressor and its turbine
The accessory gearbox and the low pressure fan
The fan and the low pressure turbine

explanation: The two spools are mechanically independent, each free to settle at the speed that suits the conditions.

question: Which components make up the N2 spool?

options.text: The low pressure compressor and the low pressure turbine
The high pressure compressor and the high pressure turbine
The fan and the accessory gearbox drive shaft
The fan and the low pressure turbine stage

explanation: This is the core spool, and it is the one connected to the starter and to the accessory drives.

question: Which parameter is used to set thrust on this engine?

options.text: Fuel flow
EPR
N2
N1

explanation: Fan speed is the closest available indication of the thrust actually being produced by a high bypass engine.

question: Which spool drives the accessory gearbox?

options.text: N1
Both spools
An air turbine
N2

explanation: The core spool turns whenever the engine is running at any useful speed, which makes it the reliable drive for the accessories.

question: Which of the following is driven by the engine accessory gearbox?

options.text: The APU generator and the APU starter motor
The pneumatic starter turbine and the start valve
The integrated drive generator and the engine hydraulic pump
The air conditioning pack fan and the recirculation fan

explanation: Electrical and hydraulic power are mechanical extractions from the engine, in the same way that bleed air is a pneumatic extraction.

question: Which spool does the pneumatic starter turn?

options.text: N1
Both spools
The fan only
N2

explanation: Turning the core is what builds compression, and N1 then follows as airflow through the engine increases.

question: Where is exhaust gas temperature sensed on this engine?

options.text: At the exhaust nozzle exit plane
At the compressor inlet guide vanes
In the fan duct downstream of the fan
Downstream of the high pressure turbine

explanation: The probes sit where the gas is hottest after doing work on the high pressure turbine, which is the condition that limits turbine life.

question: Which EGT limit is the most restrictive?

options.text: The reverse thrust limit
The start limit
The maximum continuous limit
The takeoff limit

explanation: The engine is cold and the airflow is low during a start, so the permitted temperature is lower than in any other phase. Verify the values against your operator FCOM.

question: For how long is the takeoff EGT limit normally permitted?

options.text: Two minutes
Five minutes
Ten minutes
Thirty minutes

explanation: The limit is a time restricted rating, with an extension available in some cases after an engine failure. Verify against your operator FCOM.

question: How is an exceeded engine limit displayed to the crew?

options.text: The affected parameter is displayed in red
The parameter is removed from the display
The parameter flashes in white on the display
An amber chevron appears beside the parameter

explanation: Colour coding makes an exceedance visible instantly without the crew having to recall the numerical limit.

question: What does the electronic engine control do?

options.text: It monitors engine vibration and oil parameters for the crew only
It controls the thrust reversers and the start valve
It meters fuel and controls the engine to achieve the commanded thrust
It positions the thrust levers automatically in flight

explanation: The crew commands thrust with the levers, and the control unit decides what fuel flow and schedules will deliver it.

question: What are the two operating modes of the electronic engine control?

options.text: Manual and automatic
Normal and alternate
Ground and flight
Primary and standby

explanation: The alternate mode is the degraded mode used when the normal control inputs are unavailable.

question: What is the key difference in alternate mode?

options.text: The engine can only be operated at idle thrust
Thrust reverse becomes unavailable in flight
Fuel is metered mechanically with no electronics
The control no longer uses air data inputs

explanation: Without air data the control cannot compensate for conditions the way it normally does, so thrust must be set with more care.

question: Why must thrust be set carefully in alternate mode?

options.text: Because the autothrottle commands maximum thrust
Because the protection against exceeding limits is reduced
Because the engine reverts to a fixed fuel flow
Because the thrust levers become inoperative above idle

explanation: A lever position that was safe in normal mode may produce a different result, so the indications are monitored rather than trusted to the schedule.

question: What does an ENGINE CONTROL light indicate?

options.text: Low oil pressure in the engine sump
A thrust reverser that is not fully stowed
A fault in the electronic engine control system
An exceeded EGT limit on that engine

explanation: It reports the health of the control system itself, which may still be controlling the engine acceptably.

question: Why does the electronic engine control select a higher idle when the flaps are extended for landing?

options.text: To provide more bleed air for both air conditioning packs
To reduce the time needed to spool up to go around thrust
To reduce engine vibration at low airspeed on the approach
To reduce fuel consumption on the approach

explanation: Acceleration from a low idle takes several seconds, and on short final that time is not available.

question: What is the source of the N1 limit displayed to the crew?

options.text: The electronic engine control alone
The air data computer only
The thrust lever angle set
The flight management computer

explanation: The computed limit accounts for the phase, the conditions and any derate, which is what makes a single lever position meaningless without it.

question: What is the purpose of a reduced thrust takeoff?

options.text: To allow a higher takeoff weight from the same runway length in hot conditions
To reduce the takeoff distance required on a contaminated runway
To extend engine life by using less than full rated thrust when performance permits
To reduce the noise footprint around the departure airport only

explanation: Turbine life is strongly affected by temperature, so every takeoff made at a lower rating is a direct saving in maintenance cost.

question: How many igniters does each engine have?

options.text: One
Two
Three
Four

explanation: A second igniter provides redundancy for starting and for continuous ignition in adverse conditions.

question: What are the positions of the engine start switch?

options.text: GRD, OFF, CONT and FLT
ON, OFF and AUTO
GRD, FLT and OFF
START, OFF and CONT

explanation: Each position reflects a different combination of starter and ignition requirements.

question: What does the GRD position of the start switch do?

options.text: It opens the start valve and energises the ignition
It arms the automatic start sequence only
It motors the engine without any ignition
It provides continuous ignition without the starter

explanation: Air is admitted to the starter and the igniters are energised, which is the combination a ground start requires.

question: At approximately what N2 does the start switch normally release from GRD?

options.text: 25 percent
40 percent
56 percent
70 percent

explanation: The starter is cut out once the engine is self sustaining. Verify the figure against your operator FCOM.

question: At approximately what N2 is fuel normally introduced during a ground start?

options.text: 10 percent
25 percent
40 percent
56 percent

explanation: Enough airflow must be established first so the fuel burns without an excessive temperature rise. Verify against your operator FCOM.

question: What is meant by maximum motoring?

options.text: The highest stable N2 the starter can produce before fuel is introduced
The N2 at which the start valve closes automatically during the start
The idle speed reached after a successful engine start
The maximum permitted starter operating time in a cycle

explanation: Introducing fuel at the highest available airflow gives the coolest and most reliable light up.

question: What controls the flow of fuel into the engine at the start lever?

options.text: The fuel crossfeed valve
The wing spar valve only
The engine fuel shutoff valve
The hydromechanical unit

explanation: The lever gives the crew a positive means of introducing and cutting fuel, independent of the automatic control.

question: What defines a hot start?

options.text: N2 stagnating below the idle speed after light up
Failure of the engine to light within the expected time
EGT approaching or exceeding the start limit during the start
An EGT rise before any fuel has been introduced

explanation: It means the fuel being burned is producing more heat than the airflow can carry away, and the start must be cut.

question: What defines a hung start?

options.text: The engine lights but N2 stagnates below idle
The engine fails to light at all after fuel
The start valve fails to close at the normal N2
The EGT exceeds the start limit during the start

explanation: The engine has fuel and combustion but not enough energy to accelerate, so it sits in a condition it cannot recover from.

question: Which of the following requires the start to be discontinued?

options.text: Oil pressure rising slowly towards the normal range
N1 rotation beginning before fuel is introduced
No EGT rise within the expected time after fuel is introduced
Illumination of the start valve open light during the start

explanation: Fuel entering a hot engine without lighting is fuel accumulating where it must not be allowed to accumulate.

question: What is the purpose of a dry motoring run?

options.text: To test the ignition system before a start
To warm the oil before a start in cold weather conditions
To ventilate the engine and clear fuel without ignition
To verify the thrust reverser interlocks work

explanation: It moves air through the engine to remove accumulated fuel or vapour before another start is attempted.

question: What restricts repeated engine start attempts?

options.text: A maximum APU bleed air pressure at the start valve inlet
A maximum of two start attempts per flight leg
A minimum fuel temperature between the attempts
A starter duty cycle limiting operating and cooling times

explanation: The starter overheats if run continuously, so operating and cooling periods are specified. Verify the figures against your operator FCOM.

question: What does the CONT position of the start switch provide?

options.text: Ignition on one igniter only during the start
Automatic relight if the engine flames out
Continuous starter operation during the climb
Continuous ignition without operating the starter

explanation: It keeps a source of ignition available when conditions make a flameout more likely, such as heavy rain or turbulence.

question: When is continuous ignition typically selected?

options.text: Only during an in flight engine restart attempt at altitude
In heavy precipitation, turbulence or when anti-ice is in use
During the cruise at high altitude only in winter
Whenever the autothrottle is engaged in flight

explanation: It costs nothing and removes the dependence on the engine relighting itself if combustion is momentarily disturbed.

question: What is the function of the ignition select switch?

options.text: It selects which igniter or igniters are used
It selects continuous or intermittent ignition
It selects between the two engine start switches
It arms the automatic start sequence

explanation: Alternating the igniters between flights spreads the wear and confirms both remain serviceable.

question: How is the thrust reverser on each engine actuated?

options.text: Electrically
Mechanically
Pneumatically
Hydraulically

explanation: Hydraulic power gives the force and the speed needed to translate the cowl quickly at high engine speeds.

question: How does the thrust reverser redirect the airflow?

options.text: Blocker doors deflect the fan flow through cascade vanes
The exhaust nozzle closes and reverses the core flow
Clamshell doors close across the entire exhaust
The fan blades reverse their pitch in the duct

explanation: Reversing the fan flow is sufficient because the fan produces most of the thrust on a high bypass engine.

question: What prevents a reverse thrust lever from being raised?

options.text: An interlock that requires the forward thrust lever to be at idle
A minimum airspeed interlock on the reverser sleeve actuator
A minimum N2 interlock on the affected engine only
A weight on wheels signal from the main gear only

explanation: Deploying a reverser at high forward thrust would be both structurally severe and control critical.

question: What does an amber REVERSER light indicate?

options.text: Reverse thrust is being applied normally
The reverser is not in its commanded position
The reverser has been deactivated for dispatch
Hydraulic pressure to the reverser is low

explanation: An unstowed reverser is a serious aerodynamic and asymmetric problem, so its position is monitored independently of the lever.

question: What normally governs the reduction of reverse thrust during the landing roll?

options.text: A speed by which reverse is reduced towards idle
The autobrake setting that has been selected
A fixed time interval after touchdown
The remaining runway distance displayed

explanation: Reverse is reduced before the airflow into the inlet becomes disturbed at low speed. Verify the speed against your operator FCOM.

question: Why is reverse thrust reduced at low ground speed?

options.text: To prevent the autobrakes from disengaging early
Because the hydraulic pressure falls at low engine speed
To avoid re-ingesting exhaust gas and debris into the engine
Because the reversers cannot be stowed below that speed

explanation: At low speed the reversed flow can curl forward into the inlet, carrying hot gas and loose material with it.

question: What type of oil system does each engine have?

options.text: A system supplied from the hydraulic reservoirs
A self contained system with its own tank
A shared system supplied from a central reservoir
A total loss system replenished before each flight

explanation: Independence means an oil problem on one engine has no effect on the other.

question: What is the purpose of the fuel and oil heat exchanger?

options.text: It cools the fuel before it reaches the nozzles
It cools the oil while warming the fuel
It transfers heat from the hydraulics to the fuel
It warms the oil during a cold weather start

explanation: Two problems are solved by one device, since the oil needs cooling and the fuel needs protection against ice crystals.

question: What does a red LOW OIL PRESSURE light indicate?

options.text: Oil pressure has fallen below the minimum for continued operation
The oil filter is bypassing because it is blocked
The oil temperature has exceeded its maximum operating limit
The oil quantity is below the dispatch minimum level

explanation: Loss of oil pressure will destroy the bearings within a short time, which is why it is annunciated at warning level.

question: Which oil indication gives the earliest warning of a developing leak?

options.text: Oil temperature, read at the same points
Oil pressure, read at the same points
Oil quantity, when trended across the flight
Engine vibration, read at the same points

explanation: Pressure and temperature stay normal until the loss is severe, whereas a falling quantity is visible long before that point.

question: What does the engine vibration indication monitor?

options.text: The airframe buffet felt at high angles of attack during a turn
The pulsation of the fuel supply reaching the injectors
The oscillation of the thrust reverser cowls in flight
The level of mechanical vibration produced by the rotating assemblies

explanation: A rising trend can reveal fan blade damage or an imbalance before any other parameter changes.

question: Besides oil, what else does engine oil cool on this installation?

options.text: The hydraulic system reservoir
The pneumatic pre-cooler unit
The integrated drive generator
The bleed air duct casing

explanation: The drive unit is an oil cooled machine, which is why oil temperature indications relate to both the engine and the electrical system.

question: What does the engine fire switch do when pulled, besides arming the extinguishing system?

options.text: It shuts down the engine electronically through the engine control unit without any other action
It closes the engine fuel shutoff valve at the start lever position only
It closes the fuel spar valve, closes the bleed and hydraulic shutoffs and trips the generator
It isolates the engine from the fuel crossfeed manifold and nothing else

explanation: Every flow into or out of the engine is cut at once, which starves the fire of fuel, hydraulic fluid and air.

question: What is the difference between the start lever and the fire switch as a means of shutting down an engine?

options.text: The fire switch also isolates fuel at the spar and cuts hydraulic, bleed and electrical connections
There is no practical difference between the two methods in normal service
The start lever cuts the fuel supply faster than the fire switch ever does in normal operation
The fire switch stops the engine without cutting off the fuel supply at all

explanation: A normal shutdown only needs the fuel cut, whereas a fire requires the whole engine to be isolated from the airframe.

question: What is the purpose of the fuel spar valve?

options.text: It allows fuel to be jettisoned from the wing tanks
It selects between the main and the centre tanks
It isolates fuel at the wing spar before it reaches the engine
It regulates the fuel pressure reaching the engine inlet

explanation: Cutting the supply at the wing means no fuel remains in the line running through the pylon to feed a nacelle fire.

question: Why does an engine failure also produce a hydraulic and electrical loss?

options.text: Because the fire switch trips automatically on failure
Because the hydraulic reservoirs lose their bleed pressurisation
Because the bus tie breakers open on engine failure
Because the engine drives a hydraulic pump and a generator

explanation: An engine failure is never only a thrust problem, which is why the drill covers the systems that engine was supporting.

question: What is the significance of a windmilling engine after a failure?

options.text: It provides enough thrust to maintain level flight
It prevents an in flight restart from being attempted
It supplies full hydraulic pressure from the engine driven pump
The rotation continues to drive the accessories at a reduced rate

explanation: Airflow keeps the spools turning, which is what makes a relight possible and keeps some accessory drive available.

question: What is the main advantage of a starter assisted in flight restart over a windmilling restart?

options.text: It requires no ignition to be selected by the crew
It works at lower airspeeds and produces a more reliable light up
It can be used above the maximum APU operating altitude in the cruise
It avoids the need to open the engine fuel shutoff valve

explanation: A windmilling start depends on having enough airspeed to turn the core, which may require a descent the crew would rather avoid.

question: What does the crew monitor during an engine start?

options.text: N2, EGT, fuel flow and oil pressure
N1, N2, oil pressure and oil quantity
N1, EGT, oil pressure and oil temperature
N1, N2, EGT, fuel flow and oil pressure

explanation: Each parameter confirms a different stage of the start, and a start is only successful when all of them settle at idle values.

question: Where is the APU located?

options.text: In the wing centre section above the tanks
In the tail cone, aft of the rear pressure bulkhead
In the lower forward fuselage beside the equipment bay
In the aft cargo compartment behind the bulkhead

explanation: Placing it outside the pressure vessel keeps its noise, heat and fire risk away from the occupied cabin.

question: What does the APU provide?

options.text: Electrical power only
Bleed air and electrical power
Hydraulic and electrical power
Bleed air only in flight

explanation: Supplying both is what allows the airplane to be fully independent of ground services.

question: At what speed does the APU operate?

options.text: At a speed set by the electrical load
At a speed set by the bleed demand
At idle until a load is applied
At a constant speed once running

explanation: Constant speed is what allows its generator to produce a constant frequency without a separate drive unit.

question: How is the APU started?

options.text: Pneumatically, from the ground air cart at the stand
By a cartridge starter fitted in the tail cone
By an air turbine driven from the left pneumatic duct
Electrically, by a starter motor supplied from the DC system

explanation: Its independence from any air source is what lets it be started on battery power alone with nothing connected.

question: From which tank is the APU normally supplied with fuel?

options.text: The centre tank
The right main tank
Whichever the crossfeed selects
The left main tank

explanation: A fixed source keeps the feed arrangement simple and predictable during ground operations.

question: How is APU fuel supplied when no AC boost pump is operating?

options.text: By a DC powered fuel pump
By suction from the APU fuel unit
By the left engine driven pump
By gravity feed from the wing tank

explanation: The APU must be startable with only the battery available, so its fuel supply cannot depend on AC power.

question: What are the positions of the APU switch?

options.text: OFF, ON and START
START, RUN and STOP
OFF, AUTO and MANUAL
OFF, RUN and BLEED

explanation: The start position is momentary, with the switch returning to the running position by itself.

question: What is the purpose of the APU air inlet door?

options.text: It vents the tail cone compartment in flight
It equalises pressure across the rear bulkhead
It provides cooling air to the aft cargo compartment
It admits air for the APU when it is operating

explanation: The door is closed in flight when the APU is not running, which reduces drag and keeps the compartment sealed.

question: Which APU capability is available to the highest altitude?

options.text: Bleed and electrical power
Bleed air for engine start
Electrical power
Bleed air for the packs

explanation: Electrical generation is less demanding on the APU than bleed extraction, so its altitude ceiling is higher. Verify the figures against your operator FCOM.

question: What altitude limitation applies specifically to starting the APU?

options.text: A maximum altitude for the start attempt
No limit, the APU may be started at any altitude
A minimum altitude below which it cannot be started
A limit only when the battery is the sole source

explanation: Starting requires the APU to accelerate on its own in thin air, so the ceiling for a start is lower than for continued running. Verify against your operator FCOM.

question: Why is a cooling period recommended before shutting the APU down after bleed use?

options.text: To allow internal temperatures to stabilise and prolong APU life
To allow the inlet door to close fully before the shutdown
To allow the fuel lines to drain back to the tank
To allow the APU generator to be load shed automatically

explanation: An immediate shutdown after heavy bleed extraction leaves hot sections soaking without airflow. Verify the period against your operator FCOM.

question: Which condition causes the APU to shut down automatically?

options.text: An overspeed condition
Selection of the isolation valve
A high electrical load
Loss of one bleed user

explanation: Protective shutdowns respond to conditions that would damage the unit, and they act without waiting for the crew.

question: How does APU fire protection differ between ground and flight?

options.text: In flight the APU shuts down automatically, on the ground it does not
Automatic shutdown occurs in both cases without crew action
On the ground the APU shuts down automatically, in flight the crew must act
The APU cannot be shut down at all while a fire is detected

explanation: Unattended on the ground the APU must protect itself, whereas in flight the crew may still need what it is supplying.

question: What does an APU LOW OIL PRESSURE light indicate?

options.text: That the APU has exceeded its EGT start limit
That the APU oil quantity is below the servicing level
A condition that will prevent or terminate APU operation
That the APU generator has been disconnected

explanation: As with any turbine, oil pressure is a condition of operation rather than an advisory item.

question: What does the APU FAULT light indicate?

options.text: That the APU is being started from the flight deck panel
That the APU generator is off the transfer bus
A fault that has caused or will cause an automatic shutdown
That the APU bleed valve has been closed again

explanation: It directs the crew to the reason the unit stopped, which matters when deciding whether a restart is appropriate.

question: Why is the APU EGT monitored during the start?

options.text: Because it sets the bleed air pressure available to the starter
Because it determines when the APU generator can be selected on line by the crew
Because it indicates the position of the APU air inlet door flap
Because an excessive temperature indicates an abnormal start that must be terminated

explanation: The same start problems that affect a main engine can affect the APU, and the temperature is where they show first.

question: What is the operational value of the APU after an engine generator failure in flight?

options.text: It can only supply the standby buses in flight
It can restore full electrical power to both transfer buses
It can supply hydraulic power to replace the engine pump
It can provide thrust to offset the drag of the failed engine

explanation: Restoring the lost source removes the load shedding and the single source restrictions for the rest of the flight.

question: What is required before the APU bleed air can be used for an engine start?

options.text: External power must be connected to the airplane
The APU must be running and stabilised with its bleed valve open
Both packs must be selected OFF and the isolation valve closed
The engine start switch must already be selected to GRD

explanation: The duct has to be charged and stable before the starter valve is opened, or the start will be slow and hot.

question: Why are the packs normally switched off for an engine start using APU bleed?

options.text: To make the full bleed supply available to the starter
To reduce the electrical load on the APU generator
To prevent smoke from entering the cabin during start
Because the packs cannot operate with the isolation valve open

explanation: Sharing the APU output between the packs and the starter produces a slower start with higher temperatures.

question: Why is the engine start monitored even though the control system manages the sequence automatically?

options.text: Because the starter must be cut out manually at the idle speed by the crew
Because the crew must set the fuel flow manually throughout the entire start sequence
Because the crew must terminate the start if a limit is approached or the sequence stalls
Because the control system does not monitor the EGT during the start

explanation: Automation manages the normal case, and the crew exists to recognise and stop the abnormal one.

question: What happens to the APU bleed valve when engine bleed air is selected on the same side?

options.text: The configuration is annunciated so the crew can avoid supplying the duct from both sources
The APU bleed valve is forced open so as to share the duct load equally
The engine bleed valve is inhibited until the APU has been shut down and the door closed
The isolation valve closes automatically in order to separate the ducts

explanation: The warning exists because feeding the same duct from two sources can drive air back towards the APU.
